statement.text:
An automorphism φ of a group G is called a nil-automorphism if, for every
a ∈ G, there exists n such that [a, n φ] = 1. Here [x, 1 y] = [x, y] and [x, i+1 y] =
[[x, i y], y]. An automorphism φ is called an e-automorphism if, for any two φ-invari-
ant subgroups A and B such that A ̸⊆ B, there exists a ∈ A \ B such that [a, φ] ∈ B.
Is every e-automorphism of a group a nil-automorphism?                 V. G. Vilyatser
